claim: BirA* and BioID2 biotin ligases resulted in no detectable biotinylation in zebrafish embryos as assessed by streptavidin western blotting.
source: Initial attempts using BirA* or BioID2 biotin ligases in vivo in zebrafish were unsuccessful and resulted in no detectable biotinylation in zebrafish embryos as assessed by streptavidin western blotting (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and described in the text.

claim: BASU, TurboID, and miniTurbo showed greatly improved catalytic efficiency and enhanced proximity labelling in cultured cells.
source: In recent years, the new bioID biotin ligases, BASU, TurboID, and miniTurbo, have been developed and showed greatly improved catalytic efficiency and enhanced proximity labelling in cultured cells (Branon et al., 2018; Ramanathan et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Branon et al., 2018; Ramanathan et al., 2018).

claim: TurboID injected embryos exhibited the strongest biotinylation of endogenous proteins among the three new biotin ligases with 500 μM biotin incubation.
source: TurboID injected embryos exhibited the strongest biotinylation of endogenous proteins among the three new biotin ligases with 500 μM biotin incubation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B comparing BASU, TurboID, and miniTurbo.

claim: BASU and miniTurbo were expressed at a lower level than TurboID despite equal amount of RNA injection.
source: Of note, BASU and miniTurbo were expressed at a lower level than TurboID despite equal amount of RNA injection.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation from western blot data.

claim: Greater instability of miniTurbo has been reported previously.
source: While we did not explore the underlying reasons for this, greater instability of miniTurbo has been reported previously and other biotin ligases have shown poor expression in cell cultures (May et al., 2020; Branon et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (May et al., 2020; Branon et al., 2018).

claim: Two prominent bands consistently detected around 70 and 135 kDa in all samples likely represent endogenously biotinylated proteins.
source: Note the two prominent bands consistently detected around 70 and 135 kDa in all samples likely represent endogenously biotinylated proteins (Housley et al., 2014; Ahmed et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation and citations to published literature (Housley et al., 2014; Ahmed et al., 2014).

claim: Zebrafish embryos are able to tolerate a biotin concentration as high as 800 μM with no obvious morphological abnormalities.
source: From our initial experiments with BirA*, we knew that zebrafish embryos are able to tolerate a biotin concentration as high as 800 μM with no obvious morphological abnormalities (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Weak labelling could be seen with 50 μM biotin, increasing through 250 μM, with the strongest labelling at concentration of 500 and 750 μM.
source: Weak labelling could be seen with 50 μM biotin, increasing through 250 μM, with the strongest labelling at concentration of 500 and 750 μM (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: TurboID did not produce detectable exogenous biotinylation without the addition of biotin.
source: Unlike its application in cultured cells and yeast (Branon et al., 2018), TurboID did not produce detectable exogenous biotinylation without the addition of biotin (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and comparison with published literature (Branon et al., 2018).

claim: A higher biotin concentration resulted in more TurboID in the total protein extracts.
source: Unexpectedly, the anti-Myc immunoblot showed that a higher biotin concentration resulted in more TurboID in the total protein extracts (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The addition of exogenous biotin did not change the level of endogenous biotinylated proteins in the WT embryos.
source: Concomitantly, the addition of exogenous biotin did not change the level of endogenous biotinylated proteins in the WT embryos (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: A 10-min biotin incubation with TurboID is sufficient to visualise biotinylated proteins by immunoblotting and to perform analysis of different organellar proteomes in mammalian cell culture.
source: In mammalian cell culture, a 10-min biotin incubation with TurboID is sufficient to visualise biotinylated proteins by immunoblotting and to perform analysis of different organellar proteomes (Branon et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature (Branon et al., 2018).

claim: Rapid biotinylation in zebrafish was not observed within the first 2 hr of biotin incubation.
source: However, we did not observe rapid biotinylation in zebrafish within the first 2 hr of biotin incubation (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: TurboID-induced biotin labelling was only weakly detected after 4–6 hr incubation and adequate biotinylation was only detected after overnight incubation (18 hr).
source: TurboID-induced biotin labelling was only weakly detected after 4–6 hr incubation and adequate biotinylation was only detected after overnight incubation (18 hr).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from time-course experiments.

claim: TurboID fusion proteins produced a biotinylation pattern corresponding to the appropriate subcellular location of targeting sequences/proteins in zebrafish embryos.
source: After biotin treatment, the TurboID fusion proteins produced a biotinylation pattern corresponding to the appropriate subcellular location of targeting sequences/proteins in zebrafish embryos (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The T-tubule structure was clearly visible by NeutrAvidin staining in the embryos expressing Cavin4b-TurboID.
source: The spatial resolution of the biotin labelling was remarkable as even the T-tubule structure, which is difficult to resolve in fixed embryos, was clearly visible by NeutrAvidin staining in the embryos expressing Cavin4b-TurboID.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation from immunostaining data.

claim: The biotinylated protein derived from each TurboID construct gave rise to a unique barcode of protein bands on the streptavidin blot, indicative of proteins specific to each corresponding subcellular compartment.
source: Furthermore, the biotinylated protein derived from each TurboID construct gave rise to a unique barcode of protein bands on the streptavidin blot, indicative of proteins specific to each corresponding subcellular compartment (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: TurboID was able to specifically label a selective subpopulation of endogenous proteins when targeted to a specific subcellular region or protein in zebrafish embryos.
source: These results demonstrated that TurboID was able to specifically label a selective subpopulation of endogenous proteins when targeted to a specific subcellular region or protein in zebrafish embryos.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing specific biotinylation patterns.

claim: The TurboID-biotinylated proteins were recoverable from crude fish lysates by affinity purification with streptavidin-conjugated beads.
source: Moreover, the TurboID-biotinylated proteins were recoverable from crude fish lysates by affinity purification with streptavidin-conjugated beads (Figure 2D), ready for downstream applications such as identification by mass spectrometry.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: A GFP-binding peptide (GBP; a 14 kDa nanobody) is able to target a peroxidase (APEX2) to GFP-tagged POIs in both cell culture and zebrafish systems.
source: Previously, we demonstrated that a GFP-binding peptide (GBP; a 14 kDa nanobody) is able to target a peroxidase (APEX2) to GFP-tagged POIs in both cell culture and zebrafish systems (Ariotti et al., 2015b), and can be used for ultrastructural localisation.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature (Ariotti et al., 2015b).

claim: When expressed at low levels, mRuby2-GBP showed clear colocalisation with Cavin1a-Clover at the plasma membrane in the mRuby2-positive muscle cells.
source: When expressed at low levels, mRuby2-GBP showed clear colocalisation with Cavin1a-Clover at the plasma membrane in the mRuby2-positive muscle cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: When mRuby-GBP was expressed at higher levels, red fluorescence was observed in the cytoplasm in addition to the plasma membrane, likely due to the saturation of binding between GBP and GFP.
source: However, when mRuby-GBP was expressed at higher levels, red fluorescence was observed in the cytoplasm in addition to the plasma membrane, likely due to the saturation of binding between GBP and GFP.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation and inference about the mechanism.

claim: A conditionally stabilised GFP-nanobody (destabilised GBP or 'dGBP') is rapidly degraded unless the GFP-binding site is occupied.
source: As a solution, we substituted the GBP with a conditionally stabilised GFP-nanobody (destabilised GBP or 'dGBP') that is rapidly degraded unless the GFP-binding site is occupied (Tang et al., 2016; Ariotti et al., 2018a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Tang et al., 2016; Ariotti et al., 2018a).

claim: Tight association of mRuby2-dGBP and Cavin1a-Clover was observed in all muscle cells regardless of expression level.
source: Using this approach, we observed tight association of mRuby2-dGBP and Cavin1a-Clover in all muscle cells regardless of expression level (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In embryos co-expressing ubiquitous TurboID-dGBP and tissue-specific GFP, TurboID-catalysed biotinylation was detected in the intersegmental vessels and the spinal cord motor neurons in the kdrl:EGFP and MotoN:EGFP lines, respectively.
source: In embryos co-expressing ubiquitous TurboID-dGBP and tissue-specific GFP, TurboID-catalysed biotinylation was detected in the intersegmental vessels and the spinal cord motor neurons in the kdrl:EGFP and MotoN:EGFP lines, respectively (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The TurboID-dGBP system can produce biotinylation with tissue specificity.
source: These results demonstrate that our TurboID-dGBP system can produce biotinylation with tissue specificity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing tissue-specific biotinylation.

claim: Clear colocalisation between biotinylated proteins and Clover-tagged cavins was observed in muscle fibres, at the sarcolemma and T-tubules.
source: With the same procedures, we observed clear colocalisation between biotinylated proteins and Clover-tagged cavins in muscle fibres, at the sarcolemma and T-tubules, suggesting our TurboID-dGBP system can produce proximity-dependent biotinylation with subcellular resolution.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation from immunostaining data.

claim: Without biotin treatment or without the expression of GFP, there was no detectable biotinylation effected by TurboID.
source: Without biotin treatment or without the expression of GFP, there was no detectable biotinylation effected by TurboID.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from control experiments.

claim: The specificity of GFP-directed biotinylation was not compromised in fish lines expressing higher levels of TurboID-dGBP.
source: Notably, the specificity of GFP-directed biotinylation was not compromised in fish lines expressing higher levels of TurboID-dGBP (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the absence of Cavin1a-Clover, a weak biotinylation was still observed in the embryos carrying only the TurboID-dGBP transgene, despite the level of TurboID-dGBP being undetectable on anti-Myc immunoblot.
source: Intriguingly, in the absence of Cavin1a-Clover, a weak biotinylation was still observed in the embryos carrying only the TurboID-dGBP transgene, despite the level of TurboID-dGBP being undetectable on anti-Myc immunoblot.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observation from western blot data.

claim: Background labelling is likely caused by TurboID-dGBP en route to proteasomal degradation.
source: This background labelling is likely caused by TurboID-dGBP en route to proteasomal degradation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observation of weak background biotinylation.

claim: MS analysis revealed background proteins are mainly endogenous biotinylated proteins, nuclear proteins, cytoskeletal proteins and yolk proteins.
source: Subsequent MS analysis revealed these background proteins are mainly endogenous biotinylated proteins, nuclear proteins, cytoskeletal proteins and yolk proteins (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: Endogenous Cavin4b, a known Cavin1 interactor, was detected in the streptavidin pulldown in addition to Cavin1a-GFP and TurboID-dGBP.
source: Using streptavidin affinity pulldown, biotinylated proteins were isolated from total fish lysates and endogenous Cavin4b, a known Cavin1 interactor (Bastiani et al., 2009), was detected in the streptavidin pulldown in addition to Cavin1a-GFP and TurboID-dGBP (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and citation to published literature (Bastiani et al., 2009).

claim: 26, 22, and 25 proteins were identified in the Cavin1a, Cavin4a, and Cavin4b samples, respectively, after subtracting background proteins and common containments.
source: After subtracting background proteins and common containments, 26, 22, and 25 proteins were identified in the Cavin1a, Cavin4a, and Cavin4b samples, respectively (Figure 5B and C, Supplementary file 1 – Tables 1-3).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5B and C and Supplementary file 1.

claim: The majority of proteins identified are associated with the plasma membrane, consistent with the membrane localisation of cavins.
source: Among the proteins identified, the majority of proteins are associated with the plasma membrane, consistent with the membrane localisation of cavins (Figure 5D, Supplementary file 1 - Table 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data and GO annotation shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Endogenous cavins were consistently detected in all samples.
source: Endogenous cavins were consistently detected in all samples, suggesting that the GFP-tag, as well as the binding of TurboID-dGBP, did not interfere with the oligomerisation of the cavins.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data and inference about protein function.

claim: Dystrophin (DMD), a protein associated with caveolae, was identified uniquely in the Cavin1a sample.
source: Dystrophin (DMD), a protein associated with caveolae was identified uniquely in the Cavin1a sample (Song et al., 1996; Doyle et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data and citations to published literature (Song et al., 1996; Doyle et al., 2000).

claim: An ortholog of Pacsin3 (zgc:91999), a caveola-associated protein required for muscle caveolar formation, was detected uniquely in the Cavin4b sample.
source: An ortholog of Pacsin3 (zgc:91999), a caveola-associated protein required for muscle caveolar formation (Seemann et al., 2017), was also detected uniquely in the Cavin4b sample.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data and citation to published literature (Seemann et al., 2017).

claim: Known interactors were undetectable in all control samples, demonstrating the high accuracy of the BLITZ system.
source: These known interactors were undetectable in all control samples, demonstrating the high accuracy of the BLITZ system.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing specific detection of known interactors.

claim: Caveolin1 and Caveolin (isoform unassigned) were detected in the Cavin1a sample based on two high confidence peptides but were not classified as significant hits based on the 1% global FDR analysis.
source: Note that, Caveolin1 (Uniprot accession: Q6YLH8) and Caveolin (isoform unassigned; Uniprot accession: A1L1S3) were detected in the Cavin1a sample based on two high confidence peptides (HLNDDVVK and VWVYSGIGFESAR) that were not present in the controls (Supplementary file 2) but were not classified as significant hits based on the 1% global FDR analysis.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: The poor accessibility of caveolins may reflect that a large proportion of caveolins are buried in the plasma membrane.
source: This may reflect the poor accessibility of caveolins, as a large proportion of caveolins are buried in the plasma membrane (Ariotti et al., 2015a).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observation and citation to published literature (Ariotti et al., 2015a).

claim: BLITZ does not require extensive molecular biology steps to produce numerous expression constructs, or laborious embryonic manipulation.
source: Firstly, BLITZ does not require extensive molecular biology steps to produce numerous expression constructs, or laborious embryonic manipulation.
evidence: The claim is based on the design and implementation of the BLITZ system.

claim: BLITZ relies on simple crossing of a TurboID-dGBP line with an existing GFP-tagged fish line of choice.
source: It instead relies on simple crossing of a TurboID-dGBP line with an existing GFP-tagged fish line of choice; a plethora of such lines currently exist in stock centres globally and, with the advent of nuclease directed genome editing, this number is rapidly increasing.
evidence: The claim is based on the design and implementation of the BLITZ system and knowledge of available resources.

claim: BLITZ enables cell- and tissue-specific proteomic studies, since the stability of TurboID-dGBP is dependent on its binding to GFP targets.
source: Secondly, BLITZ enables cell- and tissue-specific proteomic studies, since the stability of TurboID-dGBP is dependent on its binding to GFP targets.
evidence: The claim is based on the design principle of the BLITZ system using conditionally stabilised dGBP.

claim: Non-specific biotin labelling in tissues that do not express GFP-tagged constructs is avoided in BLITZ.
source: Non-specific biotin labelling in tissues that do not express GFP-tagged constructs is avoided.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the design principle of the BLITZ system.

claim: The TurboID-dGBP system has the potential to be used with knock-in fish lines carrying a GFP fusion protein at the endogenous locus of a POI.
source: Thirdly, our TurboID-dGBP system has the potential to be used with knock-in fish lines carrying a GFP fusion protein at the endogenous locus of a POI.
evidence: The claim is speculative about potential future applications of the BLITZ system.

claim: BLITZ will enable the application of BioID to study proteomic associations with endogenous proteins, which has not been achieved by conventional BioID methods.
source: This will enable the application of BioID to study proteomic associations with endogenous proteins, which, to our knowledge, has not been achieved by conventional BioID methods.
evidence: The claim is speculative about potential future applications and compares with existing methods.

claim: The modularity of the BLITZ system could be advantageous for use in established tissue culture systems using existing GFP expression vectors or/and knock-in cell lines, as well as extended to other organisms.
source: Finally, the modularity of the BLITZ system could be advantageous for use in established tissue culture systems using existing GFP expression vectors or/and knock-in cell lines, as well as extended to other organisms.
evidence: The claim is speculative about potential future applications of the BLITZ system.

claim: The indirect binding in BLITZ increases the physical distance between biotin ligase and the POI, which could potentially enlarge the effective labelling radius and include more non-interacting neighbouring proteins.
source: Unlike the traditional BioID approach using a direct fusion of the biotin ligase with the bait protein, our system targets TurboID to the POI through the binding of dGBP nanobody to GFP. In this case, the indirect binding increases the physical distance between biotin ligase and the POI, which could potentially enlarge the effective labelling radius and include more non-interacting neighbouring proteins.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the design of the BLITZ system and potential consequences.

claim: The use of a GFP-directed nanobody to target APEX2 for protein localisation does not appear to compromise the fidelity of labelling: APEX2 staining was rarely observed beyond 25 nm from the site of POI.
source: However, we have previously shown that the use of a GFP-directed nanobody to target a genetically encoded peroxidase (APEX2) for protein localisation does not appear to compromise the fidelity of labelling: APEX2 staining was rarely observed beyond 25 nm from the site of POI (Ariotti et al., 2015a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature (Ariotti et al., 2015a).

claim: The binding of the biotin ligase-nanobody with the GFP-tagged POI could perturb the localisation of the POI, either by masking interacting surfaces or simply due to the larger size of a complex.
source: It is also possible that the binding of the biotin ligase-nanobody with the GFP-tagged POI could perturb the localisation of the POI, either by masking interacting surfaces or simply due to the larger size of a complex.
evidence: The claim is speculative about potential limitations of the BLITZ system.

claim: BLITZ is problematic for the identification of interactors that are endogenously biotinylated, such as carboxylases.
source: As BLITZ uses biotin as a label, the method (like most BioID methods) is problematic for the identification of interactors that are endogenously biotinylated, such as carboxylases.
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge of the limitations of biotin-based labeling methods.

claim: All BioID methods will label proteins within a small number of nanometres, so non-interacting proteins could be detected simply due to close proximity.
source: In addition, as all BioID methods will label proteins within a small number of nanometres, non-interacting proteins could be detected simply due to close proximity.
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge of how BioID methods work.

claim: Subsequent validation using other independent approaches such as biomolecular fluorescence complementation and affinity pulldown is essential to distinguish bona fide interactors from non-interacting neighbouring proteins.
source: Thus, subsequent validation using other independent approaches such as biomolecular fluorescence complementation and affinity pulldown is essential to distinguish bona fide interactors from non-interacting neighbouring proteins.
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge of best practices for validating protein-protein interactions.

claim: Cavin family proteins are key components of the caveolar coat complex associated with the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane.
source: Cavin family proteins are key components of the caveolar coat complex associated with the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about cavin proteins.

claim: Cavin1 is present in all tissues and is essential for caveolar formation and function.
source: Cavin1 is present in all tissues and is essential for caveolar formation and function.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about Cavin1.

claim: Cavin2, 3, and 4 show more restricted tissue distributions with Cavin4 being specific to skeletal and cardiac muscle.
source: Cavin2, 3, and 4 show more restricted tissue distributions with Cavin4 being specific to skeletal and cardiac muscle (reviewed in Parton et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a review article (Parton et al., 2018).

claim: In the zebrafish, Cavin1 and 4 are each duplicated such that four loci exist; Cavin1a/b and Cavin4a/b.
source: In the zebrafish, Cavin1 and 4 are each duplicated such that four loci exist; Cavin1a/b and Cavin4a/b.
evidence: The claim is based on knowledge of zebrafish genetics.

claim: Cavin1a and b show spatially distinct expression patterns with Cavin1b being largely restricted to the developing notochord whereas Cavin1a, 4a, and 4b are all highly expressed in skeletal muscle.
source: Cavin1a and b show spatially distinct expression patterns with Cavin1b being largely restricted to the developing notochord whereas Cavin1a, 4a, and 4b are all highly expressed in skeletal muscle (Hill et al., 2008; Lo et al., 2015; Housley et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Hill et al., 2008; Lo et al., 2015; Housley et al., 2016).

claim: The majority of proteins identified for all cavin proteomes were muscle-enriched factors and plasma membrane proteins.
source: The majority of proteins identified for all cavin proteomes were muscle-enriched factors and plasma membrane proteins.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data analysis.

claim: A specific enrichment of known caveola-associated proteins was observed consistent with initial expectations.
source: We also saw a specific enrichment of known caveola-associated proteins consistent with initial expectations.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data analysis.

claim: The cavin proteomes contained a disproportionate number of nuclear proteins, such as Gnl3, Naca, and Lbr.
source: Interestingly, the cavin proteomes also contained a disproportionate number of nuclear proteins, such as Gnl3, Naca, and Lbr.
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data analysis.

claim: In cultured cells, cavins have been shown to be released from the plasma membrane in response to external stimuli (such as mechanical stress) and are able to bind intracellular targets in variety of subcellular locations to regulate processes such as ribosomal RNA transcription and apoptosis.
source: In cultured cells, cavins have been shown to be released from the plasma membrane in response to external stimuli (such as mechanical stress) and are able to bind intracellular targets in variety of subcellular locations to regulate processes such as ribosomal RNA transcription and apoptosis (Liu and Pilch, 2016; McMahon et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Liu and Pilch, 2016; McMahon et al., 2019).

claim: In the absence of Cavin1, in knockout mouse muscle, Cavin4 has been shown to localise predominantly to the nucleus rather than the sarcolemma.
source: In addition, in the absence of Cavin1, in knockout mouse muscle, Cavin4 has been shown to localise predominantly to the nucleus rather than the sarcolemma (Lo et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature (Lo et al., 2015).

claim: Loss of Cavin1 causes lipodystrophy and muscular dystrophy in humans.
source: We know that loss of Cavin1 causes lipodystrophy and muscular dystrophy in humans.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about Cavin1 function.

claim: Patient and animal muscle shows hypertrophied muscle fibres in Cavin1 deficiency.
source: Patient and animal muscle shows hypertrophied muscle fibres (Hayashi et al., 2009; Rajab et al., 2010; Ding et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Hayashi et al., 2009; Rajab et al., 2010; Ding et al., 2017).

claim: Cavin4 mutations have been described in dilated cardiomyopathy patients.
source: Cavin4 mutations have been described in dilated cardiomyopathy patients and there is evidence that Cavin4 recruits ERK in cardiomyocytes (Rodriguez et al., 2011; Ogata et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Rodriguez et al., 2011; Ogata et al., 2014).

claim: There is evidence that Cavin4 recruits ERK in cardiomyocytes.
source: Cavin4 mutations have been described in dilated cardiomyopathy patients and there is evidence that Cavin4 recruits ERK in cardiomyocytes (Rodriguez et al., 2011; Ogata et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Rodriguez et al., 2011; Ogata et al., 2014).

claim: There is supporting data for the positive regulation of hypertrophy in skeletal muscle fibres by Cavin1, and in cardiomyocytes by Cavin4.
source: Thus, there is supporting data for the positive regulation of hypertrophy in skeletal muscle fibres by Cavin1, and in cardiomyocytes by Cavin4.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the cited literature about Cavin1 and Cavin4 functions.

claim: The cavin proteome showed an enrichment of protein kinases, such as calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII).
source: The cavin proteome showed an enrichment of protein kinases, such as calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data analysis.

claim: CaMKII regulates Ca2+ signalling and plays an important role in the development of cardiac hypertrophy through the ERK signalling pathway.
source: CaMKII regulates Ca2+ signalling and plays an important role in the development of cardiac hypertrophy through the ERK signalling pathway (Illario et al., 2003; Cipolletta et al., 2010; Cipolletta et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature (Illario et al., 2003; Cipolletta et al., 2010; Cipolletta et al., 2015).

claim: The activation of CaMKII can be induced by exercise in skeletal muscle, with the activation level proportional to the intensity of exercise.
source: The activation of CaMKII can be induced by exercise in skeletal muscle, with the activation level proportional to the intensity of exercise (Rose et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature (Rose et al., 2006).

claim: BLITZ revealed several putative cavin interactors that have also been shown to be involved in cardiomyopathies and/or skeletal myopathies, including the membrane protein Dystrophin, the triad-associated proteins Bin1, Cypher/ZASP, and SPEG.
source: In this study, BLITZ revealed several putative cavin interactors that have also been shown to be involved in cardiomyopathies and/or skeletal myopathies, including the membrane protein Dystrophin (Deconinck and Dan, 2007), the triad-associated proteins Bin1 (Nicot et al., 2007), Cypher/ZASP (Selcen and Engel, 2005), and SPEG (Agrawal et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data and citations to published literature (Deconinck and Dan, 2007; Nicot et al., 2007; Selcen and Engel, 2005; Agrawal et al., 2014).

claim: Genetic ablation of zebrafish Cavin4b causes aberrant T-tubules in skeletal muscle.
source: Genetic ablation of zebrafish Cavin4b causes aberrant T-tubules in skeletal muscle (Housley et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to published literature (Housley et al., 2016).

claim: It is possible that Cavin4 may be involved in T-tubule formation through interaction with triad associated proteins, such as Bin1.
source: It is possible that Cavin4 may be involved in T-tubule formation through interaction with triad associated proteins, such as Bin1.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the identified interactions and known functions.

claim: The BLITZ system enables the in vivo identification of protein interactors in a cell- and tissue-specific manner, with high precision.
source: Overall, our BLITZ system enables the in vivo identification of protein interactors in a cell- and tissue-specific manner, with high precision.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results demonstrating the capabilities of BLITZ.

claim: The applicability of BLITZ was demonstrated in diverse cell types including neurons and vascular endothelial cells.
source: We demonstrated the applicability of this approach in diverse cell types including neurons and vascular endothelial cells and applied the BLITZ system to identify factors associated with cavin family proteins in differentiated skeletal muscle.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing biotinylation in different cell types.

claim: BLITZ provides a versatile and valuable tool for proteomic discovery using the zebrafish model.
source: BLITZ provides a versatile and valuable tool for proteomic discovery using the zebrafish model, but also has the potential for application in other in vivo contexts that to date have been challenging or intractable.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the demonstrated capabilities and potential applications of BLITZ.

claim: BLITZ has the potential for application in other in vivo contexts that to date have been challenging or intractable.
source: BLITZ provides a versatile and valuable tool for proteomic discovery using the zebrafish model, but also has the potential for application in other in vivo contexts that to date have been challenging or intractable.
evidence: The claim is speculative about potential future applications of BLITZ.
